title: File:Oso Landslide aerial.jpg
author: Mark Reid, USGS
description: Oblique aerial photograph of the 2014 landslide in northwest Washington. This image shows the entire extent of the landslide source area and path. This event is commonly named the “Oso Landslide” in many official reports. It is also referred to as the “SR530 Landslide,” as named by Snohomish County and Washington State. Credit: Mark Reid, USGS

title: File:2014 Washington Landslide.jpg
author: Jonathan Godt, U.S. Geological Survey
description: A photo from an aerial survey showing the upper parts of the landslide that occurred in northwest Washington state, near Oso, on March 22, 2014. USGS landslide specialists, in collaboration with seismologists and state agencies, are still working to interpret the complex sequence of events that led to the landslide. To get a perspective on the size of the landslide, look toward the bottom-left of this photo and you'll see, what appears to be, a tiny house just inside the tree line. You can read the latest updates on the science and how the USGS is contributing to the understanding of this event at on.doi.gov/OsoLandslide. Credit: Jonathan Godt, USGS.

title: File:2014 Landslide in Washington State.jpg
author: U.S. Geological Survey
description:
Photograph from an aerial survey showing the extent and impacts from the landslide in northwest Washington that occurred on March 22, 2014. The survey was conducted by the Washington State Department of Transportation, Washington State Department of Natural Resources, USGS, and King County Sheriff's Office.
Location: Oso, WA, USA
Date Taken: 3/24/2014
Photographer: Air Support Unit , King County Sheriff's Office

Read a story online about the landslide in Washington on March 22, 2014 at on.doi.gov/OsoLandslide
